correctness.rationale: Kummer borrow counts permit a digit-by-digit T_d(z) transition for the valuation distribution of binomial coefficients. Strict digitwise monotonicity of A_{p,alpha}(n) reduces a second minimum on [N,pN) to elementary rows N+p^j or 2N (for p>=3). The displayed transition product yields closed borrow polynomials for N, N+1, 2N and N+p^j. Exact truncation to valuations below alpha and exhaustive comparisons across h<alpha, h=alpha and h>alpha prove the nine-row table including all binary exceptions and odd-prime ties. Independent direct integer-binomial checks were run for small p,alpha,h and reproduced all minimum positions; this does not replace symbolic all-parameter comparisons.
residual_risks: Only nonzero coefficient counts modulo p^alpha on the stated digit-length block; higher-ranked minima not covered.
